Pandoc/Quarto math quote render test

Select part of the definition below, including a formula, and save the annotation. Two different values come out of that. The browser's capture goes into the annotation's TextQuoteSelector and is used only for anchoring; this fixture loads no MathJax, so that capture is the literal \(…\) markup you see below, where on the published Pandoc document it would be the flattened rendering ιA:C.A→C …. Separately, at intake, h's normalization service fetches this page server-side, extracts the authored TeX from its <span class="math"> markup, and stores it as the annotation's normalized_quote (method='html'). The sidebar displays that stored value and nothing else: it does no reconstruction, recovery, or OCR of its own when the annotation is shown, and it never reads the selector of a saved annotation.

What to look for. The sidebar quote should typeset the formulas that appear below only as \(…\) source — a subscripted ι_A and a script 𝒞 — sitting inline within the sentence rather than each breaking onto its own line.

Definition 2.4 (Intersection of classifiers) For classifiers \(\iota_A \colon \mathcal C.A \to \mathcal C\) and \(\iota_B \colon \mathcal C.B \to \mathcal C\) their intersection is the pullback in \(\mathbf{Cat}\) \[ \mathcal C.A \times_{\mathcal C} \mathcal C.B \longrightarrow \mathcal C, \] the category of objects carrying both structures compatibly. It is again a classifier. Iterating gives the intersection of any finite family.
